title: Alphabet in “Stijl letters”
lede: Van Doesburg’s capital alphabet of about 1919, built only from thick horizontal and vertical strokes on a square module.
summary: Capitals A to Z from thick right-angled strokes, with no curves or diagonals. Theo van Doesburg, about 1919.

source.label: Wikimedia Commons: Theo van Doesburg, Alphabet

made: About 1919 (Commons, after the Hoek catalogue; the 1968 exhibition dated the photograph 1918–1919)

evidence.note: Inspected the Commons image (3774 × 579 px, viewed at 1920 px), scanned from Joost Baljeu, *Theo van Doesburg* (1974), pp. 108–109. The object is a photograph of the alphabet, 3.5 × 17 cm, in the Centraal Museum Utrecht on loan from the Dutch State (RCE inventory AB5936).

styles.note: The rubric’s rectilinear capitals at their source: every letter is made from horizontal and vertical strokes only.

context: Commons describes the object as “Alfabet in ‘Stijlletters’”, a photograph made in Leiden, inherited by Nelly van Doesburg in 1931 and given to the Dutch State by Wies van Moorsel in 1981. [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Typeface_Theo_van_Doesburg.jpg).
The Foundry’s digital typeface [Architype Van Doesburg](https://www.thefoundrytypes.com/fonts/architype-van-doesburg/) revives the alphabet.
observed: Twenty-six capitals, A to M in the top row and N to Z in the bottom row, in solid black on white.
Every stroke is horizontal or vertical and of the same thickness; there are no curves or diagonals.
Letters that normally need diagonals, such as K, M, N, V, W, X, Y, and Z, are rebuilt from right-angled steps.
Counters are small rectangles; the letters are nearly square and set with narrow gaps.
Faint text from the facing book page shows through at the right.
interpretation: The alphabet applies the painting rule to type: no curves and no diagonals. Legibility suffers for letters such as K, X, and Z, which is the known cost of the approach.
The same letterforms appear in van Doesburg’s [poster design for La Section d’Or](ref:van-doesburg-section-dor-poster-design-1920).
borrow: Build display capitals from one stroke weight on a square grid, and replace diagonals with right-angled steps.
Keep such letters for short words; use a plain sans-serif for running text.

images.alt: Two rows of black capital letters A to Z on white, each built only from thick horizontal and vertical strokes, with square counters and no curves or diagonals.
images.caption: Theo van Doesburg, alphabet in Stijl letters, about 1919, as reproduced in Baljeu (1974). Image from [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Typeface_Theo_van_Doesburg.jpg), public domain.

rights.statement: Commons marks the image public domain. Van Doesburg died in 1931, so the design is public domain in the Netherlands; made about 1919, it is public domain in the United States under either the pre-1931 publication rule or the life-plus-70 rule. The scan is a plain reproduction of a two-dimensional work.
